# Quran Akademie — Full Reference


> Quran Akademie offers live 1-on-1 online Quran classes for children and adults in Germany, in English and German. Certified tutors (male and female teachers available), lessons scheduled in Germany time (CET/CEST, after-school and evening slots), and a free trial class with no payment details required. Courses: Noorani Qaida, Quran Reading with Tajweed, Hifz-ul-Quran, Tafseer & Understanding, and Islamic Studies for Kids. Plans: Basic $35/month (4 classes/week, 25 min), Standard $59/month (5/week, 30 min), Hifz Intensive $99/month (5/week, 45 min).

## Key facts

- **Offer:** Live 1-to-1 Quran lessons online (Zoom/Google Meet), 1-on-1 with a certified tutor — not group classes. Free 30-minute trial class; instant start (no waiting list).
- **Audience:** Muslim families in Germany; children (ages 4+) and adults; beginners through advanced (Hifz/Ijazah path).
- **Languages:** Lessons in English, German, Urdu, or Arabic (per the free-trial booking form).
- **Scheduling:** Germany time (CET/CEST), after-school and evening slots 3–8pm plus weekend mornings; fits the German school day (Ganztagsschule) and Bundesländer holidays.
- **Plans (USD, EUR equivalent at checkout):** Basic $35/month — 4 classes/week × 25 minutes; Standard $59/month — 5 × 30 minutes (most popular); Hifz Intensive $99/month — 5 × 45 minutes with a dedicated Hifz tutor. Sibling discount 10% (see pricing page).
- **Learning timelines (report consensus):** Noorani Qaida 3–6 months; children's reading fluency 12–18 months; adults learning to read 6–12 months; Tajweed accuracy a further 6–12 months; full memorisation (Hifz) 3–6 years. Hifz pace: half a page a day ≈ 3.3 years; one page a day ≈ 20 months.
- **The Quran:** 114 surahs, 6,236 verses, 30 juz, 604 pages (Medina Mushaf).
- **Germany context:** 6.6–7.0 million Muslims in Germany in 2025 (8.0–8.5% of the population), per BAMF Research Report 55 (June 2026); Turkish origin is the largest group (39.4%), followed by Arabic-speaking MENA backgrounds (28.4%).
- **Safeguarding:** Tutors are background-checked and safeguarding-trained; parents stay nearby during children's lessons; tutors never contact children privately; lessons are recorded only with consent.
- **What Quran Akademie is not:** not a mosque school (Koranschule) and not a group-class academy — online 1-on-1 lessons complement mosque schooling; not a self-study app — every lesson is live with a tutor.

## Courses

- [Noorani Qaida](https://onlinekoran.de/courses/noorani-qaida): First steps in reading Arabic — the 28 letters, harakaat (fathah, kasrah, dhammah), sukoon, shaddah, tanween, joining rules — for complete beginners (ages 4+). Typical duration 3–6 months.
- [Quran Reading with Tajweed](https://onlinekoran.de/courses/tajweed): Fluent, beautiful recitation with correct pronunciation — makhraj (articulation points), sifaat, Noon Sakinah and Tanween rules (Ikhfa, Idgham, Iqlab, Izhar), ghunnah, qalqalah, madd, waqf — following Hafs 'an 'Asim.
- [Hifz-ul-Quran](https://onlinekoran.de/courses/hifz): Structured memorisation with revision cycles (sabaq/sabqi/manzil, muraja'ah), guided by an experienced Hafiz or Hafiza. Typical journey 3–6 years.
- [Tafseer & Understanding](https://onlinekoran.de/courses/tafseer): Meanings, context and lessons from the Quran, in plain language (teens & adults).
- [Islamic Studies for Kids](https://onlinekoran.de/courses/kids-islamic-studies): Salah, duas, seerah stories and good manners for children ages 5–12.

## Guides (blog)

- [How Much Do Online Quran Classes Cost?](https://onlinekoran.de/blog/how-much-do-online-quran-classes-cost): Pricing guide — our three plans in a table, what drives the price, and market ranges as published (global live 1-on-1 $30–$120/month; Hifz $120–$200/month; Berlin offers from €40/month).
- [What Age Should a Child Start Learning Quran?](https://onlinekoran.de/blog/what-age-should-a-child-start-learning-quran): Ages 4–5 for Qaida sounds and letters; 5–7 is the ideal start window; readiness signs matter more than exact age. Age-band table with lesson lengths.
- [How Long Does It Take to Learn to Read the Quran?](https://onlinekoran.de/blog/how-long-does-it-take-to-learn-quran): Timeline table — Qaida 3–6 months, kids' fluency 12–18 months, adults 6–12 months, Tajweed accuracy a further 6–12 months, Hifz 3–6 years — and the factors that change the timeline.
- [What Is Tajweed?](https://onlinekoran.de/blog/what-is-tajweed): Definition and rule families — makhraj, sifaat, Noon Sakinah rules (Ikhfa, Idgham, Iqlab, Izhar), Meem Sakinah, ghunnah, qalqalah, madd (2/4/6 counts), waqf, tarteel, Hafs 'an 'Asim.
- [Noorani Qaida Explained](https://onlinekoran.de/blog/noorani-qaida-explained): What the Qaida covers, its stages (letters → harakaat → joining → words → sentences), how long it takes (3–6 months), and the next step (Nazra reading, then Tajweed).
- [Online vs In-Person Quran Classes](https://onlinekoran.de/blog/online-vs-in-person-quran-classes): Honest comparison table — online 1-on-1 vs mosque school vs in-person tutor — across schedule, personalisation, cost, social contact, safeguarding and commute; online lessons complement mosque school.
- [How to Choose an Online Quran Teacher: 12 Questions](https://onlinekoran.de/blog/how-to-choose-an-online-quran-teacher): 12 questions — Ijazah/sanad, Tajweed qualification, experience with kids, safeguarding checks, trial class, method, languages, scheduling, progress reports, pricing transparency, cancellation, reviews.
- [How to Memorize the Quran](https://onlinekoran.de/blog/how-to-memorize-quran): Beginner's Hifz guide — sabaq/sabqi/manzil, muraja'ah revision, Juz Amma start, chunking and spaced repetition, pace table (½ page/day ≈ 3.3 years; 1 page/day ≈ 20 months).
- [How Online Quran Classes Work](https://onlinekoran.de/blog/how-online-quran-classes-work): Step-by-step — book a free trial, meet your tutor and level check, personal learning plan, live 1-on-1 lessons on Zoom/Google Meet, progress reports; what you need and Germany-time scheduling.
- [Teaching Your Child the Quran in Germany](https://onlinekoran.de/blog/teaching-kids-quran-germany): Starting early and building a routine around German school days.
- [How to Choose an Online Quran Tutor](https://onlinekoran.de/blog/choosing-quran-tutor): Ijazah, Tajweed, safeguarding checks and the trial class.
- [Tajweed Basics for Beginners](https://onlinekoran.de/blog/tajweed-basics): What Tajweed is, makhraj (articulation points), and common beginner mistakes.

## Sources cited on this site

- BAMF Research Report 55 (June 2026) — Muslims in Germany 2025: 6.6–7.0 million (8.0–8.5%).
- Quran 73:4 — "and recite the Quran with measured recitation" (tarteel).
- Sahih al-Bukhari 5027 — "The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it."
